description:
Follow-up to PKIX-tit4.4 (option (c) doc-correction shipped). The remaining question is whether the workspace's IoFailure { kind, message } shape (PKIX-2l0v.1 D3) is the right wire form long-term, or whether one of two stronger options should be taken pre-1.0:

(a) Replace format!("{:?}", kind) with a hand-maintained u8/string match table. New std::io::ErrorKind variants become a maintenance task on each stdlib bump; no silent lossy round-trip in practice (consumers without the entry emit/decode a sentinel that survives without losing fidelity).

(b) Drop the typed kind field entirely. IoFailure becomes { message: String }. Callers needing programmatic kind branching can grep the message or upgrade their oracle.

(c) [shipped via PKIX-tit4.4] Keep Debug-of-ErrorKind, but disclose the brittleness honestly in rustdoc. Currently in tree.

Workspace-level: PKIX-2l0v.1 D3 picked the { kind, message } shape; pkix-aia and pkix-truststore both follow it. Reversing to (b) is a workspace-wide breaking change. Decision wants human input because: pre-1.0 framing argues for design closure but D3 IS the design closure, and (a)/(b) reverse it. Recommendation if no human pushback within 24h: stay at (c). Cross-references PKIX-tit4.5 (which raises the question of whether IoFailure should be lifted to pkix-path); a (b) decision here would moot tit4.5 partially.
title: IoFailure wire form: decide between Debug-of-ErrorKind (current), hand-maintained u8 table, or drop kind entirely
